title: P02 follow-up: give the AdamW token embedding the same tenfold decoupled weight decay as the Muon matrices (emb wd 0.1 -> 1.0) on the 070-claude incumbent
description: P02/P15-family follow-up to the Muon weight-decay trend (1x/3x/10x = 316/327/353): raise only emb.weight's AdamW weight decay from 0.1 to 1.0 so its per-step shrinkage matches the Muon matrices' (1e-3 at peak LR); biases, LayerNorm and Muon settings are unchanged. If the 10x gain came from smaller, more plastic weights that the frozen RL AdamW can move further, the embedding (the largest-norm matrix at handoff, spectral norm ~3.3 versus 0.5-1.7 for Muon matrices under 30x) is the one matrix still barely decayed (cumulative factor ~0.77), so decaying it should give expert iteration a more movable input representation.
hypothesis: The 1x->3x->10x Muon decay gains appeared mostly in RL (RL-solved and round-4 sample accuracy rose on every seed) rather than in pretraining loss, consistent with a plasticity mechanism: RL fine-tuning uses a fixed-lr AdamW whose per-element step size is independent of weight scale, so smaller handoff weights change relatively more per RL step. The token embedding is on AdamW with wd 0.1 and ends with the largest norm (spectral ~3.3 at 30x Muon decay in 071), so RL moves it proportionally least. Decaying it at the Muon rate shrinks its norm and should raise its relative RL plasticity; because every block is pre-LayerNorm, a smaller embedding mainly changes the embedding/block-write balance of the residual stream, not the per-block input scale. Risk: 065 showed the embedding geometry is fragile for RL (Muon on emb.weight cost -35% with unchanged val loss), and 013 (AdamW wd 1.0 on everything, pre-Muon) collapsed; this change is limited to the embedding's decay, not its update rule.
expected_delta: -5 (range -60 to +30) theorems at >=7 versus 070-claude's 352.67; pretraining steps unchanged (4700-4800), final val loss within +-0.005 of 070's 0.0911/0.0913/0.0961; if the plasticity mechanism holds, RL-solved rises on at least 2 of 3 seeds versus 788/783/838; totals stay under 1150 s

arch.change: none versus 070-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary split into two groups (emb.weight at wd 1.0; biases and LayerNorm params at wd 0.1)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: Group 1: emb.weight (99x256) with weight_decay EMB_WD = 10 * WD = 1.0. Group 2: all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f), 42 tensors, weight_decay 0.1 as before. Both groups share lr (warmup + cosine over wall-clock to 0.1x), betas (0.9, 0.95). head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW.
optimizer.decay_convention: CHANGED versus 070-claude: the token embedding's decoupled AdamW decay rises from wd 0.1 to 1.0, so its per-step shrinkage lr*wd equals the Muon matrices' MUON_LR*MUON_WD at every schedule fraction (peak 1e-3 per step instead of 1e-4). Summed over ~4770 steps (mean schedule factor ~0.55) the embedding's cumulative multiplicative decay factor becomes ~exp(-2.6)=0.07 instead of ~exp(-0.26)=0.77, matching the Muon matrices. MUON_WD stays 0.1 (10x); biases/LayerNorm decay stays 0.1.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 070-claude: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 070-claude.
